before.asserts: For every integer n>=1, v_n=(n+tau^{-2})^{-1}>0, m_n=n*barX/(n+tau^{-2}), and n*v_n=n/(n+tau^{-2}) tends to 1.
before.claim: Direct multiplication of the normal likelihood and prior gives the finite-n posterior formulas used by the asymptotic comparison.

after.asserts: Completing the square yields posterior variance $v_n=(n+\tau^{-2})^{-1}$ and posterior mean $m_n=n\bar X/(n+\tau^{-2})$.
after.claim: 27 fixed n/tau/barX normal-normal models, original prior-likelihood quadrature; no asymptotic claim.

before.asserts: At sigma=1 the limit 2*Phi(z_{1-alpha/2}/sigma)-1 equals 1-alpha; for sigma>1 it is smaller and for 0<sigma<1 it is larger.
before.claim: The coverage formula recovers nominal calibration exactly in the correctly scaled case and has the asserted direction on each side.

after.asserts: Since $z>0$, the coverage in step 2.2 equals $1-\alpha$ when $\sigma=1$, is below $1-\alpha$ when $\sigma>1$, and is above $1-\alpha$ when $0<\sigma<1$.
after.claim: Six fixed z/sigma interval probabilities with alpha defined by the normal quantile; no CLT claim.

before.asserts: For every finite n and realized Delta_n, the posterior gives zero mass to (-infinity,0), while N(Delta_n,1) gives mass Phi(-Delta_n); if Delta_n<=0, the total-variation distance is at least 1/2.
before.claim: The finite-n support mismatch supplies the nonvanishing TV lower bound used in the example.

after.asserts: By [F5], the total-variation distance from $N(\Delta_n,1)$ is at least its mass on $(-\infty,0)$, namely $\Phi(-\Delta_n)$. On $\{\Delta_n\le0\}$ this bound is at least $1/2$.
after.claim: Nine fixed n/Delta models; original prior support and Gaussian negative-halfline integration verify the TV witness; no probabilistic limit claim.

before.evidence: Step 1.1 gives posterior N(x/2,1/2) and prior-predictive N(0,2), agreeing with the one-coordinate formulas.

after.asserts: Completing the square in $t$ gives conditional variance $v_i=(s_i^{-1}+n\kappa_i^2)^{-1}$ and conditional mean $m_i(x)=v_i n\kappa_i x$.
after.claim: n=i=alpha=kappa_i=1 at x=-2,0,3: independent scalar posterior/predictive quadrature; no infinite-product or l2 claim.
